requirements.title: The _get_cloud_id() method shall resolve to the accessible-resource matching a configured ATLASSIAN_OAUTH_CLOUD_ID, regardless of the resource's position in the accessible-resources list

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 3: Deterministic cloud ID resolution
vision.paraphrase: The cloud ID resolution must respect the deployment's configured site preference, selecting it from the accessible resources even if it isn't first in the list.

conops.paraphrase: When a specific cloud ID is configured, the method must search the accessible-resources list to find and select the matching site instead of unconditionally taking the first entry.

requirements.title: The _get_cloud_id() method shall fall back to the first accessible resource when no ATLASSIAN_OAUTH_CLOUD_ID is configured, preserving existing single-instance behavior

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Cross-cutting Concerns: Backward compatible by default
vision.paraphrase: Single-instance deployments with no configured cloud ID must continue working unchanged, using the first and only accessible resource as the default behavior.

conops.paraphrase: For deployments without a configured site preference, the default behavior of selecting the first resource remains intact, ensuring backward compatibility.

requirements.title: The _get_cloud_id() method shall resolve to the sole accessible resource when the token has exactly one, regardless of whether a cloud ID is configured

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Cross-cutting Concerns: Backward compatible by default
vision.paraphrase: Single-resource tokens require no conditional logic — the resolution must work correctly whether or not a cloud ID is explicitly configured.

conops.paraphrase: When only one accessible resource exists, it is selected unambiguously regardless of any configuration, covering the common single-instance case.

requirements.title: The OAuth flow shall reject, immediately after authentication, a token whose accessible resources do not include the configured cloud site, raising an error that names both the token's actual accessible site(s) and the required site

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 4: Post-auth site validation
vision.paraphrase: A new validation gate must reject wrong-site tokens before they are cached, providing an immediate, actionable error message that explicitly names both the token's actual sites and the required site.

conops.paraphrase: Immediately after token exchange, a validation step must check whether the configured site is present in the token's accessible resources and reject the token with a diagnostic error if it is not.

requirements.title: The OAuth flow shall accept and proceed to cache a token whose accessible resources include the configured cloud site

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 4: Post-auth site validation
vision.paraphrase: The post-auth validation must accept tokens that do include the configured site, allowing normal caching and operation to proceed.

conops.paraphrase: When the token's accessible resources include the configured site, validation succeeds and the normal token caching flow continues.

requirements.title: The OAuth flow shall not cache a token that fails post-auth site validation

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 4: Post-auth site validation
vision.paraphrase: Rejected tokens must not be persisted or cached, preventing a wrong-site token from being reused on subsequent requests and causing silent failures later.

conops.paraphrase: When validation rejects a token, no caching or persistence occurs, ensuring the invalid token is never reused and always requires re-authentication.
